knowledge-base.name: fw-gin
knowledge-base.triggers: Gin, gin-gonic, github.com/gin-gonic/gin, gin.Engine, gin.Context, gin.RouterGroup, gin.HandlerFunc, Go REST API, go web framework, .go gin, gin middleware, gin routing
knowledge-base.overview: Gin 1.9+ guardrails, patterns, and best practices for Go REST APIs and microservices. Covers application factory pattern, route versioning, middleware (auth, CORS, logging), request binding with go-playground/validator, standardized error responses, and graceful shutdown. Loaded automatically when agents work on Gin-based .go files.

core-principles.principle: Use a factory function to create the router; do not call gin.Default() in production without explicitly managing its middleware.
handler -> service -> repository. Handlers parse requests and write responses only. Business logic belongs in services.
Use gin.New() and attach middleware explicitly. Never rely on gin.Default() defaults in production.
All endpoints return the same JSON envelope. Never leak internal errors to clients.
Always implement OS signal handling and a configurable shutdown timeout.

guardrail.rule: Use gin.New() (not gin.Default()) in production and attach middleware explicitly.
guardrail.bad: r := gin.Default() // implicit Logger + Recovery — not production-safe

guardrail.rule: Use ShouldBindJSON (not BindJSON) so you control the error response yourself.
guardrail.bad: if err := c.BindJSON(&req); err != nil { return } // writes 400 automatically, no control

guardrail.rule: Never store business logic in handlers. Handlers call services; services contain logic.
Never return raw internal error messages to clients. Map domain errors to safe HTTP responses.
Configure ReadTimeout, WriteTimeout, and IdleTimeout on the http.Server. Never use http.ListenAndServe without timeouts.
Group routes with versioning (/api/v1). Apply auth middleware at the group level, not per-route.
Use dependency injection for all handlers. No global state.
Always include pagination for list endpoints. Never return unbounded collections.
Use binding tags (required, email, min, max, omitempty) on all request DTOs. Use pointer fields for optional partial-update fields.

knowledge-base.project-structure:
myproject/ ├── cmd/ │ └── api/ │ └── main.go # Entry point, server setup, graceful shutdown ├── internal/ │ ├── config/ │ │ └── config.go # Configuration from env vars │ ├── handler/ │ │ ├── handler.go # Handler registry struct │ │ ├── user.go # User handlers │ │ └── auth.go # Auth handlers │ ├── middleware/ │ │ ├── auth.go # JWT/Bearer auth middleware │ │ ├── cors.go # CORS middleware │ │ └── logger.go # Request logging middleware │ ├── model/ │ │ ├── user.go # Domain model + request/response DTOs │ │ └── response.go # Standardized response wrappers │ ├── repository/ │ │ ├── repository.go # Repository registry (interfaces) │ │ └── user.go # User repository implementation │ ├── service/ │ │ ├── service.go # Service registry (interfaces) │ │ └── user.go # User business logic │ └── router/ │ └── router.go # Route definitions and grouping ├── pkg/ │ ├── validator/ │ │ └── validator.go │ └── response/ │ └── response.go ├── migrations/ ├── .env.example ├── go.mod └── Makefile
Layer responsibilities: - handler/ HTTP concerns only: parse request, call service, write response - service/ Business logic, validation, orchestration - repository/ Data access, database queries - model/ Domain types, request/response DTOs, validation tags - middleware/ Cross-cutting: auth, logging, CORS, rate limiting - router/ Route registration, grouping, middleware attachment

tooling.commands:
# Initialize project go mod init myproject go mod tidy
# Run development server go run cmd/api/main.go
# Build binary go build -o bin/api cmd/api/main.go
# Run tests go test ./... go test -v -cover ./...
# Run with race detection go test -race ./...
# Lint golangci-lint run
# Generate Swagger docs (with swaggo) swag init -g cmd/api/main.go
# Database migrations (golang-migrate) migrate -path migrations -database "$DATABASE_URL" up migrate -path migrations -database "$DATABASE_URL" down
